Insist on site assessment and load analysis before deposit
Ask for Certificate of Compliance and after-sales contact
Compare hybrid vs pure off-grid based on actual KPLC outage patterns

faq.q: Do I need an EPRA-licensed installer?

faq.a: Most Nairobi homes with intermittent but available KPLC service benefit from hybrid systems that use solar first, store excess, and draw from the grid only when needed. Pure off-grid makes sense for unreliable or absent grid areas or when full independence is required.

Critical for night-time use and blackouts. LiFePO4 is strongly preferred over older lead-acid/gel for cycle life, safety and performance in Nairobi conditions. Size battery bank to cover essential loads for the number of hours of autonomy you need.

Clear workmanship warranty (typically 1–2 years), manufacturer warranties on panels (25 yr performance), inverter and batteries, remote monitoring guidance, and a reachable local contact for faults. Reputable independents stay responsive after installation.

glossary.EPRA: Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority – issues solar PV technician (T1–T3) and contractor (C1/V) licences in Kenya
glossary.Hybrid system: Solar + battery + grid interconnection that prioritises solar/battery and falls back to KPLC
glossary.LiFePO4: Lithium iron phosphate battery chemistry preferred for safety, cycle life and Nairobi temperatures
glossary.kWp: Kilowatt-peak – rated DC output of the solar array under standard test conditions
